title: Hanuman Thought Mandodari Was Sita
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 5(8-9) (Critical Edition; vulgate 5.10-11)

captions.instagram:
Did Hanuman once mistake Mandodari for Sita?

In Ravana's palace, Hanuman once mistook Queen Mandodari for Sita, and danced for joy. Then he stopped and reasoned it out: Sita, apart from Rama, would neither sleep nor adorn herself, and would go to no one but Rama, not even Indra. He recognised Sita by her character, before he ever saw her face. This moment is right there in Valmiki's Sundara Kanda.

Had you heard this moment from the Sundara Kanda before? Which Hanuman story should we tell next? 👇

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 5(8-9) (Critical Edition; vulgate 5.10-11)

Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 5(8-9) (Critical Edition; vulgate 5.10-11)
Verses:
• Searching for Sita, Hanuman entered Ravana's palace at night — 5.7.1-3
• Hanuman saw Mandodari, radiant like gold, Ravana's chief queen, asleep — 5.8.48
• By her beauty and youth he concluded 'This is Sita' and rejoiced — 5.8.49
• He clapped his arms, kissed his tail, played, sang, climbed pillars and dropped to the ground — 5.8.50
• He discarded the thought: Sita, apart from Rama, would not sleep, eat, adorn herself or drink — 5.9.1-2
• She would approach no other man, not even the lord of the gods: 'this is not she' — 5.9.3

verify_note: CE 5.8.48-50: Hanuman sees Mandodari, concludes 'This is Sita' by her beauty and youth, rejoices (arms, tail, singing, pillars). CE 5.9.1-3: he discards the thought — Sita apart from Rama would not sleep, eat, adorn herself or drink, nor approach any other, not even Indra. Mandodari is named in 5.8.48.
